Scope: Second-pass static review of the retained SSView ZLib codec source, focused on failure behavior and exact publisher terms; no DLL, viewer, or source execution

PublisherEvidence.PublishedCodecBehavior: SSView searches its directory for DLLs exporting EncodeIStream and DecodeIStream. The page identifies ZLibCodec source as a sample and says selected encoders/decoders are used when streams are saved or loaded.
PublisherEvidence.PublishedTerms: The current support page says trial or unregistered software is freeware for non-commercial usage, identifies purchased named-user/build-machine, team and site license types, and includes a software EULA. No owner-specific entitlement or redistribution determination was made.

StaticFindings.Observation: Codec exceptions are swallowed. The handler rewinds the input and appends the complete input to the memory output, but does not clear that output first. If encoding or decoding has already written partial output before raising, the returned stream can contain partial output followed by the original input; the caller receives no explicit error from this path.
StaticFindings.Confidence: Control-flow implication from source; whether the included Delphi ZLib implementation reaches this state for a specific input is unverified without execution.

StaticFindings.Observation: Nil and zero-length input return before assigning an output stream.
StaticFindings.Confidence: Direct source observation; caller handling is unknown.

StaticFindings.Observation: The sample imports Delphi ZLib and resource units; the archive does not include the referenced ZLibCodec.res file, so a reproducible build and exact dependency/license provenance are not established.

The source documents same-directory DLL discovery by two export names and confirms that stream transformations can participate in load/save. Review and acceptance must use an isolated viewer directory and disposable structured-storage copies; do not allow unrelated DLLs or user documents into the fixture.
StaticFindings.Confidence: Direct source observation, consistent with the publisher product page.
